title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the long 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' manuscript (cote 140-3, a sequel to La Longue Marche). In it Grothendieck studies objects attached to a group (scheme) G and two 'sections' rho, sigma of G. These are very plausibly elements or conjugacy data playing the role of the standard generators of the modular group (orders 3 and 2, or 6 and 4), with G of GL_2 type.

On the previous page he obtained maps M_{rho,sigma} -> T_{rho,sigma} -> T_rho, a determinant map T_{rho,sigma} -> N'_sigma -> G_m, and a map T_{rho,sigma} -> mu_2 x mu_2. He stressed that none of this used the actual sections rho, sigma, only their existence. He then announced that cube (96) is a 'composite' of two cubical diagrams.

This page draws one of them, cube (116).
- Vertices, upper face: SR_{rho,sigma}, R_{rho,sigma}, M^+_{rho,sigma}, M_{rho,sigma}. Lower face: the same objects with superscript o.
- Edges carry the structure groups of a GL_2-type 'square' of central extensions/isogenies: G_m, G, SG, PG.
  - SR -> R: G_m.
  - R -> M: PG.
  - SR -> M: G (dashed composite).
  - SR -> M^+: SG.
  - M^+ -> M: G_m.
- The square mirrors G_m -> G -> PG and SG -> G, i.e. the pullback/pushout relations among GL_2, SL_2, PGL_2 and G_m via the determinant.
- Dashed characters kappa: R -> G_m and chi: M -> G_m are drawn, related through squaring lambda -> lambda^2. The squaring reflects that det restricted to the centre G_m is lambda -> lambda^2.
- The o-versions carry characters kappa^o, chi^o.
- Vertical edges are labelled mu_2 x mu_2.

The text says (reading of difficult handwriting): as in (95)/(96), the lower face is deduced from the upper one by passing to neutral components, or to a canonical sub-object of index mu_2 x mu_2. The four finite quotient groups are isomorphic to one another via the vertical arrows, and are isomorphic to mu_2 x mu_2; this is presumably the invariant T_{rho,sigma} -> mu_2 x mu_2 of the previous page. The lateral faces of the cubes are cartesian, but apparently not the top and bottom faces. The next page (117) completes the picture with the T-objects. It shows that one lateral face is trivial, M^+ = SR x SG, and that the opposite face becomes so only after passing to pro-coverings M~ = R x SG.

Purpose: bookkeeping of the structure (torsor/extension lattice, characters, component groups) of the spaces of solutions M_{rho,sigma} of the 'loop equation' for a GL_2-type group. This prepares an attempt to recover rho, sigma from finer structure such as the n-subgroups M_{rho,sigma}(n).
errors: No mathematical error can be verified; the page is a diagram plus a short commentary whose exact meaning depends on definitions given on earlier pages, (95)-(115), which are not available.
The machine transcription garbles the prose; several labels (the 'c' superscript on SR, the '~' under M^{+o}) are uncertain.

ideas.what: Commutative cube of torsors/extensions with structure groups G_m, G, SG, PG, i.e. the GL_2/SL_2/PGL_2/G_m square, compatible with characters to G_m related by squaring.
ideas.modern_name: Diagram of central extensions/isogenies of reductive groups (det, centre, adjoint quotient) transported to torsors or representation spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard folklore of reductive group theory
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 for the group-theoretic facts; this specific cube is unpublished

ideas.what: Passage from the full spaces to neutral-component (or 'o') versions, with all four component groups canonically isomorphic to mu_2 x mu_2; the lateral faces of the cube are cartesian.
ideas.modern_name: Component group / pi_0 of representation or solution varieties; cartesian squares of torsors

ideas.what: Study of the solution spaces of the 'équation des lacets' (relations between the images of the order-2 and order-3 generators of the modular group) in GL_2-type groups.
ideas.modern_name: Character/representation varieties of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 (or SL_2(Z)) into GL_2, SL_2, PGL_2
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (e.g. work on character varieties of free products and of SL_2(Z))
ideas.where_published: The Longue Marche manuscripts are circulated but not formally published

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an intermediate bookkeeping diagram, a cube of G_m/SG/PG/G torsors with mu_2 x mu_2 component groups, within a long unpublished computation. It is technically careful but routine in content; nothing here stands out as an unknown result or connection.
transcription_corrections: Prose reading (uncertain): 'Comme dans (95) (96), la face inférieure est déduite de la supérieure en passant aux composantes neutres, les quatre groupes quotients étant isomorphes entre eux par les flèches ..., ils sont isomorphes à mu_2 x mu_2 — cf. dans le cube ci-dessous (117). Les faces latérales des cubes sont cartésiennes, mais pas les faces ...'
Page-number note at top reads '572' (as transcribed, uncertain); the symbol under M^{+o}_{rho,sigma} is likely '\wr' (isomorphism) or a pointer, not part of the label.
Vertical labels read 'mu_2 x mu_2' (as transcribed).
